directAnswer: To connect a Git merge, first ensure you are on the branch you want to merge into, then use the command `git merge <branch-name>` to merge the specified branch.
summary: This guide provides steps to connect a Git merge, including platform-specific instructions and common pitfalls.

sections.heading: Git Merge Basics
sections.body: A Git merge combines changes from one branch into another. It's essential to resolve any conflicts that may arise during this process.

sections.heading: Platform-Specific Steps
sections.body: The following steps are applicable for command line interfaces on Windows, macOS, and Linux.

steps.title: Checkout the Target Branch
steps.detail: Use the command `git checkout <target-branch>` to switch to the branch you want to merge into.

steps.title: Merge the Source Branch
steps.detail: Execute `git merge <source-branch>` to merge changes from the specified source branch.

steps.title: Resolve Conflicts
steps.detail: If there are any merge conflicts, Git will notify you. Open the conflicting files, resolve the issues, and then stage the changes with `git add <file-name>`.

steps.title: Complete the Merge
steps.detail: Finalize the merge by committing the changes with `git commit -m 'Merge <source-branch> into <target-branch>'`.

faqs.question: What should I do if I encounter merge conflicts?
faqs.answer: You need to manually resolve the conflicts in the affected files, then stage and commit the resolved files.

faqs.question: Can I undo a Git merge?
faqs.answer: Yes, you can use `git merge --abort` to cancel the merge process if you haven't committed yet.

faqs.question: Is it possible to merge multiple branches at once?
faqs.answer: No, Git does not support merging multiple branches in a single command; you must merge them one at a time.

caveats: Ensure your working directory is clean before starting a merge to avoid complications.
Merging branches with significant differences can lead to complex conflicts.
